facts.text: I've had them for a long time; they're chronic.
I haven't noticed any changes in my vision.
It has been going on for a long time.
My face looks puffy, including around my eyes.
The outer parts of my eyebrows have thinned out.
I have dyslipidemia — abnormal cholesterol and blood fats.

findings.name: skin and face inspection
findings.result: Dry skin; pale, puffy face with periorbital edema; thinning of the lateral eyebrows.

findings.name: MRI of the brain and sella
findings.result: 15 × 17 × 12 mm pituitary lesion: T1-hyperintense, T2-hyperintense, intensely enhancing with gadolinium; elevates the optic chiasm and stalk; infiltrates both cavernous sinuses.

findings.name: testosterone, LH and FSH
findings.result: Testosterone 2.04 ng/mL (NR 2–10); LH 2.8 UI/L (NR 1.24–8.62); FSH 5.1 UI/L (NR 1.27–19.26).

findings.name: thyroid ultrasound
findings.result: Atrophic, hypoechoic gland consistent with autoimmune thyroiditis.

aliases: pituitary hyperplasia due to primary hypothyroidism
pituitary hyperplasia secondary to primary hypothyroidism
gold.reasoning: 1. Consideration of thyrotrophic pituitary hyperplasia due to primary hypothyroidism — “...reduced circulating levels of thyroid hormone result in overstimulation of thyrotrophs by thyrotropin releasing hormone.” 2. Consideration of hypophysitis — “...as well as in the rare entity of hypophysitis.”

x009: Free T4 of 0 ng/dL is probably an undetectable value; kept as written.

leakage.reason: The MRI report names the organ ('pituitary lesion'), one word of the gold diagnosis; it does not name hyperplasia, and the report is kept as written.

source_issues: s009: free T4 '0 ng/dL' is not a measurable value (probably below detection).
s004: bitemporal hemianopsia on perimetry while the patient perceives no visual change (s001); consistent, but worth knowing.
notes: Index visit: the outpatient presentation with chronic headaches (s001-s011); the CT, MRI and perimetry (s002-s004) precede the review of systems in the narrative but belong to the same workup.

Signs the patient can notice (dry skin, puffy face, thinning outer eyebrows) are facts and also stay in the examination; pallor, macroglossia, bradycardia and the non-palpable thyroid are examiner findings only.
The MRI record avoids 'pituitary' in its name and aliases (gold word); a request for a pituitary MRI should match 'MRI of the brain and sella'.
